correctness.rationale: Both the original mathematical proof and the narrowed claim check out. Given the draws up to ordinary cover, last marks occupy distinct indices and remain independent with the stationary success probability; completion cannot occur earlier. The conditional residual law is independent of cover. The stationary renewal identity and unselected-subset expansion give the finite PGF and mean (take the first-order difference at z=1). The finite strict inequalities follow by strict convexity/concavity of the two log factors under majorization, with no stochastic-majorization assertion. For the repaired limit, w̄_m=1+O(1/m), so the slow-group exponential maximum yields exp(-θ exp(-x)) at time (m/a)(log m+x); the fast factor tends to one. A cover union bound and conditional interarrival variance imply an o_P(m) de-Poissonization error. In the delay transform and mean, the grouped coefficients are bounded by (2c)^{j+k}/(j!k!); the denominators after scaling converge to s+aj+bk or aj+bk respectively. The inverse limit transform is exactly the stationary-to-zero renewal resolvent of the two-class process: starting at zero its zero probability is exp(-c+C_1 e^{-at}+C_2 e^{-bt}). The repaired proof shows the transform tends to one as s decreases to zero, excluding an infinite hitting time, and its first-order term gives the same mean. The stationary time-zero mass is e^{-c}, and finite independence passes to the joint limit. Strict Jensen at positive times with weighted speed mean one proves the strict equal-rate delay comparison. An independent four-state rational solve at q=(1/3,2/3), p=1/4, z=1/2 returned E[z^D]=180/271, ED=29/18, E[z^T]=27/271, ET=46/9, matching the finite formulas.
residual_risks: The exact rational replay is one finite input; it is not the asymptotic proof. No full completion moment limit, arbitrary rate-array limit, or stochastic majorization is inferred.

The examined finite completion formula and single-rate scaling do not state or mechanically specialize to this conclusion.

originality.rationale: The original's presentation of finite strict balancing for mean completion as a distinct contribution fails: indexed record d79ee5d7e4b4 treats exactly the same nonuniform common-loss refresh model, gives the full completion transform and mean, and proves strict Schur-convexity and the unique uniform minimizer. This is established statement overlap, not a retrieval issue or an order inference from dates. Its mean minus the ordinary cover mean also gives the finite delay mean. The repaired Finding withdraws that finite contribution, retains finite identities as attributed preparation, and claims only the joint two-speed critical law, its exact limiting delay and convergent mean, and the strict speed-dispersion penalty in that limit. The checked uniform-sampling critical results have a single death rate, whether or not the loss marks are heterogeneous, and the exact nonuniform finite prior has no two-speed limit. Deriving the shifted slow-class extreme-value limit, decoupling it from the stationary two-rate hitting law, and controlling the scaled delay mean are beyond a direct parameter substitution in those results. The pass applies only to the re-audited repaired claim.

The interlacing record's primary passage was unavailable; its indexed finite scope is not treated as proof of noncoverage. value.rationale: Two positive fixed fractions are the simplest sampling heterogeneity in which rare slow first arrivals and residual missing types have different governing information. The Gumbel part sees only the slow class, while the independent queue delay sees both, even though the total average selection speed remains one. The exact transform, delay moment convergence and strict comparison measure a heterogeneity effect that the ordinary cover law or the finite total mean alone does not characterize. This is meaningful without a general rate-distribution theorem. The replacement mathematical statement and slogan were inspected and preserve the source evidence.
residual_risks: The effect is a post-cover delay comparison, not a comparison of centered Gumbel locations or a stochastic ordering of full collection times.
